html:
Xinjiang is the huge dry region of northwest China, split by the Tian Shan mountains into Dzungaria in the north and the Tarim Basin in the south. The map shows it from 1914 to 1945, when it was a province of the Republic of China that the central government barely controlled.

The Qing won the region in the 1750s after they destroyed the Dzungars, and made it a province in 1884. The name means "new frontier". Its oasis towns had been stops on the Silk Road for two thousand years, and most of its people were Turkic-speaking Muslims, the Uyghurs and Kazakhs.

After the 1911 revolution a string of warlords ran Xinjiang as their own state:

  • Yang Zengxin, 1912 to 1928, kept it quiet and apart. He was assassinated.
  • Jin Shuren, 1928 to 1933, provoked a large Muslim revolt. A short-lived East Turkestan Republic rose in the south in 1933 and 1934.
  • Sheng Shicai, 1933 to 1944, ruled with Soviet troops and advisers behind him.

A second East Turkestan Republic held the north from 1944 until the People's Republic took over in 1949.
